articles.title: Crude Oil Prices Dip 1% To $114 As US-Iran Diplomacy Raises Hopes Of De-Escalation
articles.description: Crude oil prices declined on Thursday amid renewed diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions. US crude fell 1.28%, while Brent slipped 1.02%. However, supply disruption risks persisted. The World Bank forecast Brent averaging $91 per barrel in 2026, warning that falling inventories could increase global market vulnerability

articles.title: Asian shares and U.S. futures are mixed after Google parent Alphabet's earnings disappoint
articles.description: Asian shares and U.S. futures are mixed, weighed down by some big technology stocks after Google parent Alphabet’s earnings were below expectations. As expected, the Federal Reserve kept its key rate unchanged. Oil prices fell more than 1% early Thursday, even as U.S. officials warned that renewed military action against Iran could come after the Nov. 3 midterm elections. On Wednesday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 added 0.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite climbed 0.3%. Markets are watching for the outcome of a meeting of the European Central Bank later Thursday. The Bank of Japan is expected to stand pat when it wraps up its policymaking meeting on Friday.

articles.title: Europe Faces Early Winter Stress Test as Cold Snap Forecast Pushes Natural Gas Prices Toward 100 Euros per Megawatt
articles.description: Benchmark Dutch TTF natural gas prices climbed above 97 euros per megawatt-hour on Monday, the first time at that level since the 2022 energy crisis, according to Bloomberg. The move came as meteorologists forecast temperatures across parts of continental Europe to fall 2 C to 3 C below normal starting this weekend, the report stated. […]
